You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | CPI Cooling to 3.5% Boosts Risk Appetite, AI Sector Rebounds; US-Iran Conflict Escalates Oil Supply Risks; Fed Nominee Warsh Stresses Independence & Transparency

TEXT:
I. Hot News
Federal Reserve Dynamics
June CPI YoY Slows to 3.5%, Below Expectations; Market Risk Appetite Rises
US June CPI YoY growth slowed to 3.5%, with a MoM decline of 0.4%, coming in below market expectations. Core inflation also moderated. While inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target, the cooling signal is clear.
Key points: Fed Chair nominee Kevin Warsh reaffirmed commitment to the 2% inflation anchor during congressional testimony, stressing “data dependence” and improved policy transparency. Overseas holdings of US Treasuries rose to $9.37 trillion in May, the second-highest level on record.
Market impact: Short-term relief from aggressive rate-hike fears supports growth stocks and risk assets. However, geopolitical factors could introduce new disturbances to the inflation trajectory, and the Fed is expected to remain cautious.
International Commodities
US-Iran Conflict Escalates, Hormuz Strait Tensions Rise, Crude Supply Risks Increase
The Trump administration announced the end of the US-Iran ceasefire. US forces struck Iranian targets and re-blocked ports while revoking the planned 20% transit fee for the Hormuz Strait, positioning the US as “guardian” of global energy channels.
Key points: Roughly 20% of global oil transportation passes through the strait. Trump stated actions will continue until “enough is enough,” with energy facility strikes possibly reserved for last. Iran has not issued a formal response.
Market impact: Short-term upward pressure on crude prices and energy-sector volatility, raising global inflation and supply-chain uncertainty. Safe-haven assets such as gold receive partial support, though a stronger dollar may act as a counterbalance.
Macroeconomic Policy
Warsh Hearing Emphasizes Policy Independence and Transparency; US-UK Launch Stablecoin Regulatory Cooperation
Kevin Warsh reaffirmed monetary policy independence and pledged institutional reforms to remove implicit inflation taxation, avoid premature rate-path signaling, and enhance predictability.
Key points: The US-UK “ future markets Transatlantic Working Group” released recommendations for stablecoin regulatory cooperation, creating clear pathways and removing barriers while supporting cross-border tokenized-asset testing.
Market impact: Strengthens Fed credibility and provides short-term support for the dollar and Treasury yields. A clearer stablecoin framework could benefit compliant crypto adoption and institutional inflows.
II. Market Review
Commodities Forex Performance (Real-time Update)
Spot Gold : 4,057 USD/oz, 24h +0.12%
Spot Silver : 58.93 USD/oz, 24h +0.41%
WTI Crude : 79.54 USD/bbl, 24h +1.09%
Brent Crude : 86.03 USD/bbl, 24h +1.53%
US Dollar Index (DXY) : 100.824, 24h -0.12%
Driving Factors Analysis : June CPI cooling has lifted risk appetite, yet the escalation of US-Iran geopolitical conflict has emerged as a fresh market variable. Tensions around the Hormuz Strait have heightened fears of crude supply disruptions, lending short-term support to oil prices. Gold trades in a narrow range as safe-haven demand competes with a firmer dollar and higher yields. Institutional consensus suggests that prolonged conflict could push energy-driven inflation higher, potentially delaying Fed easing and offering temporary support to the DXY while exerting pressure on precious metals. Risk assets and safe-haven instruments are clearly diverging. Short-term focus remains on how conflict developments transmit into supply chains and inflation expectations.

ETH : 1,880 USD, +5.4%

Below, long-liquidation clusters concentrate between 63,200–64,200 USD; a drop through 64,000 USD support risks cascading long liquidations. Event Overview : NVDA is exploring cooperation with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries on AI data-center cooling and energy-management systems and is partnering with SK Group on a Japan AI-factory project (2028–2029), defining next-generation data centers as “AI factories.” Market Interpretation : Institutions see this as reinforcement of NVDA’s global leadership and competitive moat in the AI infrastructure ecosystem. Expanded supply-chain collaboration supports the long-term growth narrative. Investment Insight : NVDA’s core growth story remains solid. Pullbacks may offer entry opportunities, but valuation and geopolitical risks to the semiconductor supply chain warrant attention.

Siri upgrades are advancing; the iOS 27 public beta emphasizes privacy, positioning Apple against OpenAI and Anthropic. Market Interpretation : Analysts are positive on Apple’s hardware-plus-privacy differentiation in generative AI. On-device capabilities could become a new growth vector and accelerate catch-up versus cloud-centric rivals. Investment Insight : Hardware-based AI features may catalyze valuation re-rating. Watch product launches and ecosystem partnerships; long-term allocation value remains attractive.
